item: Rollup decline kept across restarts, Home and map stop spending the statement deadline
key_paths: src/analytics/rollup_hold.py; src/analytics/rollup_serve.py; src/analytics/queries.py; src/api/insights.py; src/api/boot_sequence.py; src/briefing/card_audit.py; src/static/app-home.js; src/static/app-map.js; src/static/app-corpus.js
summary: From the 2026-10-16 diagnostics: a rollup build that DuckDB's limit stopped is kept in rollup_stopped.json (codes and numbers only) and released by a larger limit, offload becoming allowed, a corpus 5% smaller than at the stop, or another app/build version, so a restart no longer pays the 921 s scan again. The decline reason is exported (status, boot row). /trending-windows takes a 20 s live budget (shortest window first, windows it did not finish are left out and named, never cached as whole), /map gets the statement deadline, an epoch-and-filter-keyed cache and a country-list budget, a failure or partial answer is replayed for 30 s marked partial and replayed, Home backs its trends poll off per route (only a 503 or a partial answer counts), a named scan pause shows as that pause, the card audit runs rising_now last and counts skipped producers, and the parity check and benchmark compare against the build's scan bound. English partial caveats; locale keys, a build that fits the tier, month occupancy and a prune from the middle are named items in OPEN_QUEUE.
